key_insight: Coherent noise drives the triangular-lattice surface code into a partially decodable critical phase, dual to algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking in a quantum paramagnet.
engineering_relevance: The results identify a coherent-noise regime where optimal Pauli decoding retains partial recovery capability rather than exhibiting a simple recoverable-to-unrecoverable transition.
method: Analyze single-qubit Pauli-Z rotations followed by surface-code syndrome measurements.
Use Wegner duality to connect decoding to strongly symmetric decoherence in a Z₂ paramagnet.
Derive universal signatures using an SO(n) nonlinear sigma model in the replica limit n→1.
evidence_signal: Large-scale numerical simulations confirm analytical predictions for aspect-ratio-dependent optimal Pauli decoding fidelity and power-law decay of the dual fidelity correlator.
watch_item: The findings concern a specific coherent-noise model and optimal Pauli decoding; performance under realistic mixed noise and practical decoders remains to be established.
paper_title: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code
